# Other spellings of the same mistake, beyond the two this repository shipped.
# tests/test-no-credential-in-argv.sh must flag every command below.

# podman login -p, the shape of akmods' `just login` recipe.
podman login ghcr.io -u "$REGISTRY_ACTOR" -p "$REGISTRY_TOKEN"
# A long flag joined with =, its value built from Actions expressions.
buildah push --creds=${{ github.actor }}:${{ secrets.GHCR_TOKEN }} "${IMAGE}"
# --registry-password, given a quoted expression with spaces inside it.
cosign sign --registry-username "${GITHUB_ACTOR}" --registry-password "${{ github.token }}" "${IMAGE_REF}"
# A lower-case variable, read through a command substitution.
docker login -u "${actor}" --password "$(cat "${token_file}")" ghcr.io
# A token in a URL with any user name, unquoted.
git push https://oauth2:$CI_JOB_TOKEN@gitlab.example.com/group/repo.git HEAD
# printf counts only when it writes to a pipe or a file. Here its output
# becomes git's argument, so the token is on git's command line.
git clone "$(printf '%s' "https://x-access-token:${GH_TOKEN}@github.com/o/r.git")" repo
# skopeo copy and sync name the credential per side, not --creds.
skopeo copy --dest-creds "${REGISTRY_ACTOR}:${REGISTRY_TOKEN}" oci:build docker://ghcr.io/o/i
skopeo copy --src-creds=u:${{ secrets.GHCR_TOKEN }} docker://ghcr.io/o/a docker://ghcr.io/o/b
# A short flag with its value attached, no space between them.
podman login ghcr.io -u "${REGISTRY_ACTOR}" -p"${REGISTRY_TOKEN}"
# curl's user:password and an Authorization header are argv too.
curl -fsSL -u "x-access-token:${GH_TOKEN}" https://api.github.com/user
curl -fsSL -H "Authorization: Bearer ${{ github.token }}" https://api.github.com/user
curl -fsSL --header "Authorization: token ${GH_TOKEN}" https://api.github.com/user
